title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
claim: Standard residual and unconstrained multi-stream connections are unstable; adding manifold-constrained projections to the mappings yields a stable, identity-preserving variant.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right progression, colored mapping boxes (orange vs green) marking the change
description: Three gray rounded panels sit side by side, labeled (a) Residual Connection, (b) Hyper-Connections (HC) and (c) Manifold-Constrained HC (mHC). Each panel is a block diagram that reads bottom to top. Input x_l is at the bottom and output x_{l+1} is at the top, with a circled plus sign where the branches merge. Panel (a) has a single skip arrow and a blue Layer F box on a side branch. Panels (b) and (c) use stacked-card icons for the widened multi-stream residual. They add Pre, Res and Post Mapping boxes around Layer F, with intermediate states h^in, h^out, h^res and h^post. In (b) the mapping boxes are orange and use plain H notation. In (c) they are green and wrapped in a projection operator P_M. The color change from orange to green is where the eye lands first.
caption: Illustrations of Residual Connection Paradigms. This figure compares the structural design of (a) standard Residual Connection, (b) Hyper-Connections (HC), and (c) our proposed Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC). Unlike the unconstrained HC, mHC focuses on optimizing the residual connection space by projecting the matrices onto a constrained manifold to ensure stability.
abstract: Recently, studies exemplified by Hyper-Connections (HC) have extended the ubiquitous residual connection paradigm established over the past decade by expanding the residual stream width and diversifying connectivity patterns. While yielding substantial performance gains, this diversification fundamentally compromises the identity mapping property intrinsic to the residual connection, which causes severe training instability and restricted scalability, and additionally incurs notable memory access overhead. To address these challenges, we propose Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), a general framework that projects the residual connection space of HC onto a specific manifold to restore the identity mapping property, while incorporating rigorous infrastructure optimization to ensure efficiency. Empirical experiments demonstrate that mHC is effective for training at scale, offering tangible performance improvements and superior scalability. We anticipate that mHC, as a flexible and practical extension of HC, will contribute to a deeper understanding of topological architecture design and suggest promising directions for the evolution of foundational models.
